correctness.rationale: For C_{2m} stable-set P, primitive outward facet rays r_i=-e_i and s_i=e_i+e_{i+1} become signed apex/rim graph-incidence columns under bipartition sign twist, hence totally unimodular. A normal cone is nonsmooth exactly at dependent active facet rays. Feasible graph circuits are whole rim (alternating 1-dimensional face F_alt) or apex-rim path circuits; each active latter forces the four-ray cone for F_i:x_i=1. Thus singular reduced components are L=F_alt orbit closure P1 and n pairwise incomparable Y_i, each toric path stable-set of dim n-3. Their saturated primitive circuit relations yield transverse 2x2 and m x m rank-one determinantal cones, with node and binom(2m-2,m-1) multiplicities. Intersections of Y_i for nonempty S are nonempty iff S is stable; remaining induced complement-N[S] graph is disjoint paths; unimodular fence-poset equivalence and Stanley linear-extension theorem imply degree multinomial(d;d_j) prod E_{d_j}. L intersections iff S single parity, one endpoint. Independent full face incidence test on C6: 18 stable vertices, 403 nonempty faces, 7 maximal non-simplicial faces, top degrees n=6,8,10 -> 12,128,2720; not a proof for all n.

originality.rationale: Scientific best-of-knowledge assessment after independently reading the frozen RESULT.md and recreating relevant proof/calculation, checking Resultary and named primary source statements. Wagner 1996 and the Lakshmibai--Mukherjee 2007 Theorem6.9 give general Hibi singular-locus criteria, so an abstract method for locating nonsmooth orbits is PRIOR. Stanley 1986 already gives path-fence volumes Euler zigzag numbers. The claimed new synthesis is a complete even-cycle specialization with an extra singular line of different codimension, generic rank-one determinantal transverse models and complete intersection-degree formulas for all selected Y_S. General statements alone need explicit circuit/face analysis; no exact same-specialization earlier table was located in targeted searches.
